Administrators of other major centralized virtual currencies report processing similar transaction

By way of comparison, according to information reported publicly, in 2012 Western
Union made remittances totaling approximately $81 billion, PayPal processed approximately
$145 billion in online payments, the Automated Clearing House Network processed $36.9
trillion in transactions, and Bank of America processed $244.4 trillion in wire transfers.
This relative volume of transactions becomes important when you consider that,
according to the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime, the best estimate for the amount of
all global criminal proceeds available for laundering through the financial system in 2009 was
$1.6 trillion.

This pattern of rapid movement across multiple counterparties is consistent with the entity's declared business purpose as an import-export trading firm.

statutory.label: contradiction
statutory.reasoning: 31 U.S.C. § 5318(g) requires financial institutions to report transactions that are suspicious. In this fact pattern, Entity SYN_1e802910 is an import-export trading firm with a declared monthly volume of $8,322,782. The observed transactions are consistent with this business purpose and volume, and there are no indicators of fraud, money laundering, or other illicit activity. Because the activity aligns with the KYC profile, 31 U.S.C. § 5318(g) requires reporting only for suspicious transactions that are not present here.
